best_section.where: the lookout car park off Sir Samuel Griffith Drive, about 40m east of the pin

summary: Bushland pin is unreachable; nearest spot is a busy roadside lookout car park.
reasons: Pin itself sits in dense untracked forest
Nearby car park faces a through road
No houses nearby, well hidden by trees

drivers.seclusion: No dwellings or windows visible anywhere nearby; the pin is buried in bushland on Mt Coot-tha, but the only vehicle-accessible spot, a lookout car park, sits right beside Sir Samuel Griffith Drive and is fully visible to anyone driving past.
drivers.access_and_room: The pin itself has no track and can't be reached by van. The car park 40m away is sealed/gravel with clear turning room, so access there is fine.
drivers.traffic: Sir Samuel Griffith Drive is a scenic through-route up Mt Coot-tha, not a dead end, so some traffic is likely at any hour even if light overnight.
drivers.convention: Not applicable here (parking area, not a kerb); the QLD imagery shows the car park full of day-visitor cars, which doesn't tell us about overnight use.

flags: Steep surrounding terrain: mean grade 16.4%, max 38.4% nearby, though the car park itself looks flat
Likely a day-use lookout car park, possibly gated or signed against overnight stays, not visible in imagery
No streetlighting or on-site signage visible to confirm overnight rules
sun_shade: Dense eucalypt canopy shades the car park and pin from most directions; only the road-facing edge gets direct sun.
cannot_judge: Whether the car park has a gate or barrier that closes overnight
Any on-site no-camping or time-limit signage
